title: What are the square and the circle in this grid?
description: In a grid, three squares make twenty seven and two circles with a square make nineteen. The row with one kind of shape is solved first, and its value is carried into the next row. Keeko doubts that the circle is ten.
teaching_notes: One idea: solve the row with one kind of shape first, then carry its value into the next row. Watch for students who take the square away from the total and call what is left one circle, when it is two circles.

source: In a grid, three squares make 27 and two circles with a square make 19
video_script.why: A child finds the values of two shapes in a grid by solving the row with one kind of shape first and carrying its value to the next row.
video_script.substitution: the grid's own two rows, three squares making twenty seven, and two circles and a square making nineteen
video_script.anchor: a grid of two rows: three squares with the total 27, and two circles and a square with the total 19
video_script.wrong_move: takes the square away from nineteen and calls what is left one circle, when two circles are left
video_script.payoff_line: The square is nine and the circle is five.

final_answer.spoken: the square is nine and the circle is five

maths_rules: Three equal squares make 27, so one square is 27 / 3 = 9.
Two circles and a square make 19, so two circles make 19 - 9 = 10.
video_script.design: One idea: solve the row with one kind of shape first. The grid stays in the anchor band and the working sits on the working board.

narration: <bookmark mark='book'/>This question is from your book. It shows a grid with two rows of shapes.
<bookmark mark='one'/>The first row has three squares, and its total is twenty seven.
<bookmark mark='two'/>The second row has two circles and a square, and its total is nineteen.
<bookmark mark='ask'/>What number is each shape?

beats.on_screen: the grid holds still and the two totals glow

marks.think: Keeko sits at the corner of the board

narration: <bookmark mark='think'/>Think and tell.

beats.on_screen: two squares in different rows carry the same value; a card says start with the row of one kind of shape

marks.start: the card start with the row of one kind of shape appears

narration: <bookmark mark='same'/>In a grid, the same shape has the same value everywhere.
<bookmark mark='start'/>We start with the row that has only one kind of shape.

beats.on_screen: Given: three squares make 27; two circles and a square make 19

marks.given: the two rows and their totals are written

narration: <bookmark mark='given'/>Given, three squares make twenty seven. Two circles and a square make nineteen.

beats.on_screen: To find: the number for the square and for the circle

marks.find: the things to find are written

narration: <bookmark mark='find'/>We have to find the number for the square and for the circle.
<bookmark mark='three'/>Step one, three equal squares make twenty seven.
<bookmark mark='one'/>Share twenty seven into three equal parts, and one square is nine.

marks.row: 2 circles + 9 = 19 is written, with the square replaced by 9

narration: <bookmark mark='row'/>Step two, in the second row, the square is nine.
<bookmark mark='take'/>Take away nine from nineteen, and the two circles make ten.
<bookmark mark='half'/>Step three, two circles make ten, so one circle is half of ten, which is five.
<bookmark mark='one'/>Step four, check both rows. Nine plus nine plus nine is twenty seven.
<bookmark mark='two'/>Five plus five plus nine is nineteen.
<bookmark mark='ans'/>The square is nine and the circle is five.

beats.on_screen: Keeko with a raised hand; Keeko's bubble shows circle = 10; the second row is tested as 10 + 10 + 9 = 29 beside 19; the bubble is struck out

marks.test: the second row is written as 10 + 10 + 9 = 29 beside 19

narration: <bookmark mark='hand'/>Keeko has raised a hand. Let us check the doubt and solve it.
<bookmark mark='doubt'/>Keeko thinks the circle is ten, because nineteen take away nine leaves ten.
<bookmark mark='test'/>Test it. Ten plus ten plus nine is twenty nine, not nineteen.
<bookmark mark='strike'/>The ten left over is for two circles, so one circle is only half of it.
